witness.why: 6 != 1 mod 23, so the congruence fails at n = 12, which lies in the stated domain [0, 60].
witness.reason: 23 is prime, so the multiplicative group mod 23 has order 22. The order of 6 must divide 22, hence lies in {1,2,11,22}; 12 is not among them. Direct computation gives ord_23(6) = 11, not 12. Reduction of the exponent mod 12 is therefore invalid; the correct modulus for the exponent is 11.
witness.all_failures_in_domain: 49 of the 61 values n in [0,60] fail; exactly the 12 values n in [0,11] satisfy it, trivially, since there n mod 12 = n.

search_bound: Not a bounded search: the stated domain is the finite set n in [0,60] and all 61 values were checked exhaustively with exact integer arithmetic (Python arbitrary-precision ints, pow(6,n,23)). No floating point was used.
broken_step: s2 ("The residue 6 has order 12 modulo 23") is false, and it is the only step that carries the conclusion. Order 12 is impossible mod 23 by Lagrange (12 does not divide 22); the true order is 11. s2's own sub-claim, 6^(n+12) = 6^n mod 23 for n in [0,48], fails at every one of those 49 values. Steps s4, s6, s8, s9 are true but vacuous filler that never feed the conclusion, and s10 inherits s2's falsity.
